Silencing of the gene $N$ will result in a tall phenotype.
Overexpression of the gene $\boldsymbol{P}$ will have no effect on height of the plant.
Overexpression of the gene $O$ can lead to plants with tall phenotype.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for amplification of DNA fragments involves multiple cycles of thermal denaturation, annealing and extension steps in each cycle. Because of the heat denaturation step, a thermostable polymerase is required for performing PCR. An experimenter had all the resources except the thermostable DNA polymerase to perform a PCR. The experimenter can use ______ to substitute for thermostable DNA polymerase.
options: Escherichia coli DNA polymerase added before denaturation step of every PCR cycle
Escherichia coli DNA polymerase, added after extension step of every PCR cycle
excess amount of Escherichia coli DNA polymerase added once at the beginning of the reaction
Escherichia coli DNA polymerase, added after annealing step of every PCR cycle

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
In order to understand immune responses to COVID-19 viral infection, a researcher took five individuals of an animal model of the disease. One of these animals was infected, in controlled lab conditions, by nasal spray of the viral suspension. The animal developed pneumonia-like symptoms (fever and difficulty in breathing) ten days later. Blood plasma was collected at two time points from the infected animal: i. when symptoms were still there (draw 1 ), ii. seven days after the animal completely recovered from the illness (draw 2). The remaining four animals were given different treatments with the plasma (either draw 1 or draw 2), and then challenged with viral infection. Symptom development was monitored and results are tabulated. (assume the plasma is made hypoallergenic by chemical treatment)
$\begin{array}{|l|l|} \hline \text{Treatment(M, N, O or P)} & \text{Result} \\ \hline \text{(M). Injection of draw1, followed by mock spray (no virus)} & \text{only fever developed} \\ \hline \text{(N). Injection of draw 1, followed by the viral challenge} & \text{mild disease symptoms} \\ \hline \text{(O). Injection of draw 2, followed by the viral challenge} & \text{no disease symptoms} \\ \hline \text{(P). No plasma treatment before the viral challenge} & \text{severe disease symptoms} \\ \hline\end{array}$
Based on these results, the correct inference(s) would be.
options: In treatment $(\mathrm{O})$, the viral antigen from the plasma generated a humoral immune response (antibody response) in the animal and thus protected it.
In treatment $(M)$ fever was because of cytokines such as interferons that are in the plasma.
In treatment $(\mathrm{O})$ antibodies against COVID-19 gave passive immunity to the animal.
In treatment (N) symptoms were mild, because interferons from the plasma set a general innate immune state in the animal.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Conjugation in $E$. coli is a microbial process wherein conjugative plasmids are transferred from one bacterium to another that does not possess it. This requires physical contact between the cells involved in the transfer. In an experiment performed in a sterilized U-tube, strains $\mathbf{P}$ (resistance to ampicillin encoded in its plasmid) and Q (resistance to tetracycline encoded in its genome) were grown in an appropriate medium without an antibiotic. A $0.22 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ pore size nitrocellulose membrane placed in between the two arms serves as a partition. In a parallel identical experiment the $0.22 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ membrane was replaced by a $30 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ nitrocellulose membrane. After allowing enough time for the conjugation process to occur, an aliquot from each arm is plated on either ampicillin or tetracyclin antibiotic containing plate. Choose the correct statement about the outcome of the experiment.
options: Strain Q would be ampicillin resistant in experiment 1.
Strain P would be tetracycline resistant in experiment 2.
Strain Q would be ampicillin resistant in experiment 2.
Strain P would be tetracycline resistant in experiment 1.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Antibiotics P1, P2 (cell wall synthesis inhibitors), and Q1, Q2 (protein synthesis inhibitors) are equally hydrophilic and moderately toxic to humans. Staphylococcus is known to develop resistance to all these antibiotics. An experimenter tested these antibiotics against a recent pathogenic strain of Bacillus. A high density of Bacillus culture was spread on a nutrient agar plate. Filter paper discs, each soaked in P1, P2, Q1 and Q2 individually (of same concentration), were placed on the bacterial lawn (purple background in the schematic). M is mock control without any antibiotic. Following an overnight incubation, a zone of inhibition is seen around each disc, except for M. Additionally, few individual colonies were observed in zone of inhibition for P2. Based on these observations select the correct statement(s).
options: Q2 would be the preferred antibiotic for therapy against this Bacillus infection.
If P 2 is a new generation antibiotic derived from P 1 , then long term use of $\mathbf{P} 2$ is likely to remain highly effective against this Bacillus infection.
The combination of P1 and P2 will not lead to antibiotic resistance in the Bacillus.
The combination of P1 and Q2 is least likely to lead to antibiotic resistance in the Bacillus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Hydra has a receptor Q in certain cell/s that respond to a specific neurotransmitter P1, isolated from brains of higher mammals. An experimenter finds that many species have neurotransmitters that are structurally related to P 1 and have functional homologs of receptor Q . Binding of P to Q elicits neuronal response. A summary of this study is given below.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline \text{species} & \text{number of Q genes} & \text{response to P group (P1 to P4) of molecules} \\ \hline \text{Hydra} & 1 & \text{Yes (only to P1)} \\ \hline \text{Worms} & 1 & \text{Yes (only to P1)} \\ \hline \text{Insects} & 0 & \text{No response to P1, P2, P3, P4} \\ \hline \text{Fishes} & 1 & \text{Yes (only to P1)} \\ \hline \text{Amphibians} & 2 & \text{Yes (only to P1 and P3)} \\ \hline \text{Reptiles} & 3 & \text{Yes (only to P3 and P4)} \\ \hline \text{Birds} & 4 & \text{Yes (only to P3 and P4)} \\ \hline \text{Mammals} & 5 & \text{Yes (only to P1, P2, P4)} \\ \hline \end{array}$
Based on this information choose the statement(s) that is(are) likely to be correct.
options: In mammals, P3 can compete with P1, P2, P4 for eliciting the response.
Insects might have lost the gene $\mathbf{Q}$ due to the loss of endogenous production of $\mathbf{P}$ group of neurotransmitters.
Insects have lost the gene Q after fish have evolved.
In mammals, the Q gene multiplication occurred as a result of diversification of the neurotransmitter $\mathbf{P}$.

Equilibrium is reached between $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$and $\mathrm{K}^{+}$across the membrane.
Both $\mathrm{K}^{+}$and $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ion channels are open leading to more $\mathrm{K}^{+}$influx than that of $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$.
Opening of $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ion channels, leading to $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$efflux.

On an oceanic island, long isolated away from any continent, there are only four co-existing species: flowering shrub, rabbit, large deer and small fox. The food web for the island ecosystem is depicted below.


Deer and rabbit eat precisely the same parts of the flowering shrub, depleting the shrub vegetation at precisely the same rates. If predation is NOT the reason that the four species coexist, choose the statement that best explains their coexistence.
options: Deer population is large in number.
The population of small fox is larger than that of rabbit.
Interspecific competition is stronger than intraspecific competition.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
A crop variety was developed at a research station in Dehradun (located in a temperate zone) and this variety produces round ( $R R$, or $R r$ ) or wrinkled seeds ( $r r$ ) with green ( $G G$ or $G g$ ) or yellow seed $(g g)$ colour. A field test was performed with seeds from a cross between $R R G G$ (round and green) and $\operatorname{rrgg}$ (wrinkled and yellow) parents. Seeds obtained from this test were planted at the same research station and compared to three new tropical locations with different levels of microbial infection and salinity challenges.
$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|}\hline & \text{Temperate region} & \text{Tropical region} & \text{Tropical region with microbial infection} & \text{Tropical region with microbial infection and high salinity} \\ \hline \text{Number of seeds sown} & 800 & 800 & 800 & 800 \\ \hline \text{Number of seeds germinated} & 795 & 355 & 210 & 190 \\ \hline \text{Number of plants reached flowering} & 775 & 350 & 208 & 48 \\ \hline \text{Number of plants producedseeds} & 766 & 345 & 204 & 47 \\ \hline \text{Total yield} & 8.2 \mathrm{~Kg}(6.2 \text{ Kg Green} + 2.0 \text{ Kg Yellow)} & 3.6 \mathrm{Kg}(1.5 \text{ Kg Green} + 2.1 \text{ Kg Yellow)} & 2.1 \mathrm{~Kg}(0.05 \text{ Kg Green} + 2.05 \text{ Kg Yellow}) & 0.51 \mathrm{Kg}(0.01 \text { Kg Green}+0.5 \text { Kg Yellow)} \\ \hline\end{array}$
Based on the information provided and assuming that the genes follow Mendelian inheritance (with no other factors affecting the yield), choose the correct statement(s) from the options given below.
options: It is better to sow three parts of green seeds and four parts of yellow seeds in tropical region.
Wrinkled character is better suited for tropical region than round character.
Tropical region does not support the growth of round seed plants.
Only yellow seeds are better to sow in tropical region carrying high microbial infection load.

questions.subject: Biology

Barbara McClintock observed non-Mendelian pigmentation patterns in maize (figure 1) mediated by transposons, as also observed in Petunia (figure 2 and 3). These somatic changes were inheritable as evident from the clonal patterns of pigmentation observed both in seeds and flowers.


As leaves grow, 'jumping genes' get activated and insert themselves into chlorophyll producing genes, thereby disrupting and inactivating them. This is typically seen as leaf pigment variegation ( $\mathbf{P}$ and Q ). Sometimes, the transposon jumps out from where it was inserted, restoring the chlorophyll gene function. Observing the leaf variegation patterns in P and Q , choose the correct statement(s).
options: Only Q shows clonal propagation of the variegated phenotype.
Only P largely indicates that the transposon can jump out of chlorophyll gene, restoring its function.
Tissue culture propagated plants from green tissue of leaf Q will show no variegation.
Both $\mathbf{P}$ and Q show sporadic events of transposon-mediated variegation.

If $E$ is a point on the side $B C$ and $A E+D E$ is minimum, then the coordinate of $E$ is
options: $\left(\frac{5}{2}, 6\right)$
$\left(\frac{19}{8}, \frac{46}{8}\right)$
$\left(\frac{21}{8}, \frac{50}{8}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\vec{a}, \vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ be any three vectors. Then
options: $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}=0$ if $\vec{a}, \vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ are unit vectors with $\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}=0$
$\vec{a}+\vec{b}, \vec{b}+\vec{c}$ and $\vec{c}+\vec{a}$ are coplanar if $\vec{a}, \vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ are coplanar
$|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|$ if $(\vec{a}+\vec{b}) \cdot(\vec{a}-\vec{b})=0$
$\vec{a}=\vec{b}$ if $|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|$ and $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=0$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The potential for a point charge $+q$ placed at a distance $d$ from a grounded infinite conducting plate is $V(x, y, z)=k q\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x^2+y^2+(z-d)^2}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{x^2+y^2+(z+d)^2}}\right)$
Here $k=1 / 4 \pi \epsilon_0$ is a constant. The maximum value of induced charge density on the conducting plate is
options: $-2 k \epsilon_0 q / d^2$
$-k \epsilon_0 q / d^2$
$-k \epsilon_0 q / 2 d^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two point charges $q$ and $\lambda q$ in vacuum are located at the points $A(a, 0)$ and $B(\mu a, 0)$ in the xy plane. Assume that $a \gt 0$ and $q \gt 0$. Select the correct statement(s).
options: If the midpoint between the charges is fixed, then the maximum force of attraction is $\frac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_0} \lambda\left[\frac{q}{2 a}\right]^2$.
If the sum of the charges is fixed, then the maximum force of repulsion between the charges is $\frac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_0}\left[\frac{q}{a(1-\mu)}\right]^2$.
If the mid point between the charges is fixed, then the maximum force (attractive or repulsive) happens when the charges are placed symmetrically about the origin.
If the sum of the charges is fixed, then the maximum force of attraction happens when $\lambda$ is -2 .

It's given that the surface temperature of the Sun is 6000 K and assume that the Sun continues giving energy at the same rate in future. If the source of Sun's radiated energy was its gravitational potential energy instead of the nuclear fusion then the Sun will cease to exist in a time of the order of

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Thermal de Broglie wavelength is the de Broglie wavelength of the gas particles in an ideal gas at temperature $T$ with average kinetic energy given by the equipartition theorem and usual relation between kinetic energy and momentum. Consider an ideal monoatomic gas $A$ of $N_a$ atoms, each of mass $m_a$ and another ideal monoatomic gas $B$ of $N_b$ atoms, each of mass $m_b=4 m_a$. Both gases are uniformly distributed in boxes of volume $V$ at temperature $T$. Select the correct statement(s).
options: If a photon has wavelength equal to thermal de Broglie wavelength of atoms of gas $A$ then the ratio of photon momentum and average momentum of atoms in gas $A$ i.e $p_{\text {photon }} / p_A$ is $2 / 3$.
If total mass of gas $A$ is same as total mass of gas $B$ then their pressures are related as $P_B=4 P_A$.
Thermal de Broglie wavelengths of gases $A$ and $B$ are in ratio $\lambda_A / \lambda_B=2$.

If volume and temperature are such that, for both gases A and B , the average inter-particle spacing in each direction is equal to thermal de Broglie wavelength of respective atoms $\lambda_A$ and $\lambda_B$ then $N_b=8 N_a$.

questions.q: A spherical raindrop of initial mass $M_0$ and initial radius $R$ falls freely from rest. Let $\rho$ be the constant density and $r$ the radius at time $t$. Assume that the drop maintains it's spherical shape. The drop loses mass at the rate $d m / d t=-4 \pi k \rho r^2$. where $k$ is a constant. Define $t_c=\frac{R}{k}$. Select the correct statement(s)
options: The speed of the drop at time $t_c / 2$ is $15 g R / 8 k$
The rate of mass loss goes to zero as time $t \rightarrow t_c$
The drop loses all it's mass in time $t_c$
The momentum approaches $M_0 g R / 4 k$ as $t \rightarrow t_c$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Consider an optical medium where refractive index varies linearly with height i.e. $n(y)=n(0)+k y$ where $k$ is a positive constant and $y$ is the height above the ground level. Here positive number $n(0)$ is the refractive index at the ground level. The refractive index at height $y$ varies with temperature at that point as $(n(y)-$ 1) $T(y)=$ constant. Consider a ray propagating (in a plane) in the medium which is horizontal at the ground level (i.e. at grazing angle) and makes an angle $\theta$ with horizontal at height $h$ as shown in the figure. Use small angle approximation i.e. keep only terms upto and including quadratic order in all trigonometric functions. Select the correct option(s).
options: The temperature at height $h$ is greater than the temperature at ground level.
Angle $\theta=\sqrt{2\left(1-\frac{n(0)}{n(h)}\right)}$.
For $n(0)=1.001$ and $k=1 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^{-1}$, angle $\theta$ at height 1 meter above the ground level is equal to $\sqrt{1 / 5}$
Angle $\theta=\sqrt{2\left(1-\frac{1}{n(h)}\right)\left(1-\frac{T(h)}{T(0)}\right)}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A disk shaped coin is tossed up in the air with 'Head' side on the top. The initial centre of mass velocity of the coin is $6.8 \mathrm{~m} \cdot \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$ in the vertical direction. In addition, the disk is rotating about the horizontal axis with angular velocity $6 \pi \mathrm{rad} \cdot \mathrm{s}^{-1}$. Assume the motion in air is torque-free. Find the number of completed flips the disk will perform before it hits the ground under the action of gravity.
options: 5 completed flips with 'Tail' side on the top.
4 completed flips with 'Tail' side on the top.
5 completed flips with 'Head' side on the top.
4 completed flips with 'Head' side on the top.

questions.q: Two different materials $M_1, M_2$ of equal dimensions (length $L$ and uniform cross-sectional area $A$ ) having thermal conductivities $k_1$ and $k_2$ respectively are connected together through a bolt $M_3$. The bolt (length $=2 L$, area $=A / n$ ) is of another material with thermal conductivity $k_3$ such that $n \gg 1$. The left sides of the material $M_1$ and $M_3$ are kept at the temperature $T_1$ whereas the right sides of the material $M_2$ and $M_3$ are kept at the temperature $T_2$ as shown in the figure below such that $T_1 \gt T_2$. Assume that the bolt $\left(M_3\right)$ is thermally insulated from materials $M_1$ and $M_2$. The equivalent thermal resistance of this system is

$\frac{L}{\left(k_1+k_2\right) A}$
$\frac{L\left(k_3+2 n\left(k_1+k_2\right)\right)}{A\left(k_1+k_2\right) n k_3}$
$\frac{2 n L\left(k_1+k_2\right)}{A\left(2 n k_1 k_2+k_2 k_3+k_3 k_1\right)}$
